newsitem.title: POLAND: Number of Polish farms fell from 1988 to 1996.
newsitem.headline: Number of Polish farms fell from 1988 to 1996.

text.p: The number of individual farms in Poland fell to 2.04 million in 1996 from 2.17 million in 1988, the year before communism fell, according to the results of an official agricultural census held in June last year.
In a report on Tuesday the Central Statistics Office (GUS) said the average area of an individual farm, defined as one larger than one hectare, was 7.91 hectares in 1996.
This was 0.86 hectares more than in 1988, when the previous census was held.
Those farms measuring less than five hectares made up 55.3 percent of all farms, compared to 53.4 percent in 1988.
Farms larger than 10 hectares made up 15.1 percent of the total, down from 17.2 percent in 1988, but in 1996 these accounted for 54 percent of arable land compared with 46 percent previously.
In 1996 there were just over a million smallholdings measuring less than one hectare, down from 1.68 million in 1988.
Agriculture as a whole in 1996 employed 11.56 million people or 29.9 percent of Poland's population.
The area sown in the whole agricultural sector amounted to 12.3 million hectares in 1996, 14.4 percent less than in 1988. GUS estimated the area lying fallow at 1.8 million hectares.
The number of cattle amounted to 7.14 million head in 1996, 30.9 percent less than at the previous census, while there were 17.96 million pigs, down 8.4 percent.
